\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{തപാൽപ്പെട്ടി} (tapālppeṭṭi)}{തപാൽപ്പെട്ടി (tapālppeṭṭi)}]{\ml{തപാൽപ്പെട്ടി} (tapālppeṭṭi) — a post box}

\label{lesson:ML-C490-tapalppetti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to make a payment, then the Malayalam for to stand in line.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{തപാൽപ്പെട്ടി}}
\textbf{\ml{തപാൽപ്പെട്ടി}} — \emph{tapālppeṭṭi} — \textquotedblleft{}a post box\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ഞാൻ} \ml{കത്ത്} \ml{വഴിയിലെ} \ml{തപാൽപ്പെട്ടിയിൽ} \ml{ഇട്ടു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ñān kattŭ vaḻiyile tapālppeṭṭiyil iṭṭu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I dropped the letter into the post box on the road.
\end{quote}

\ml{തപാൽ}, the post, plus \ml{പെട്ടി}, a box. Post boxes are painted red.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{തപാൽപ്പെട്ടി}} (\emph{tapālppeṭṭi}) is a Malayalam compound built from \ml{തപാൽ}, the post, a word that came in through Hindustani, and the native word \ml{പെട്ടി}, a box (DEDR 4388).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tapālppeṭṭi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tapālppeṭṭi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ñān kattŭ vaḻiyile tapālppeṭṭiyil iṭṭu.} — I dropped the letter into the post box on the road.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to make a payment, then the Malayalam for to stand in line, then say \emph{tapālppeṭṭi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{തപാൽപ്പെട്ടി} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A post box\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{കൊറിയർ} (koṟiyar)}{കൊറിയർ (koṟiyar)}]{\ml{കൊറിയർ} (koṟiyar) — a courier}

\label{lesson:ML-C490-koriyar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to stand in line, then the Malayalam for a post box.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{കൊറിയർ}}
\textbf{\ml{കൊറിയർ}} — \emph{koṟiyar} — \textquotedblleft{}a courier\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{പുസ്തകങ്ങൾ} \ml{കൊറിയറിൽ} \ml{ഇന്നലെ} \ml{എത്തി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pustakaṅṅaḷ koṟiyaṟil innale etti.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The books came by courier yesterday.
\end{quote}

It names both the company and the parcel it brings.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{കൊറിയർ}} (\emph{koṟiyar}) was borrowed from English \emph{courier}, a firm that delivers parcels.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{koṟiyar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{koṟiyar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pustakaṅṅaḷ koṟiyaṟil innale etti.} — The books came by courier yesterday.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to stand in line, then the Malayalam for a post box, then say \emph{koṟiyar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{കൊറിയർ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A courier\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{കൈപ്പറ്റുക} (kaippaṟṟuka)}{കൈപ്പറ്റുക (kaippaṟṟuka)}]{\ml{കൈപ്പറ്റുക} (kaippaṟṟuka) — to receive officially; to take receipt of}

\label{lesson:ML-C490-kaipparruka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a post box, then the Malayalam for a courier.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{കൈപ്പറ്റുക}}
\textbf{\ml{കൈപ്പറ്റുക}} — \emph{kaippaṟṟuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to receive officially; to take receipt of\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ഓഫീസിലെ} \ml{ഗുമസ്തൻ} \ml{എന്റെ} \ml{അപേക്ഷ} \ml{കൈപ്പറ്റി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ōphīsile gumastan enṟe apēkṣa kaippaṟṟi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The office clerk received my application.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{കൈപ്പറ്റി}, \emph{kaippaṟṟi}.

Literally to take into the hand: \ml{കൈ} plus \ml{പറ്റുക}, to get hold of. Common on forms and receipts.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{കൈപ്പറ്റുക}} (\emph{kaippaṟṟuka}) is a native Dravidian compound of \ml{കൈ}, the hand (DEDR 2023), and \ml{പറ്റുക}, to take hold of (DEDR 4034).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaippaṟṟuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaippaṟṟuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ōphīsile gumastan enṟe apēkṣa kaippaṟṟi.} — The office clerk received my application.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a post box, then the Malayalam for a courier, then say \emph{kaippaṟṟuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{കൈപ്പറ്റുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To receive officially; to take receipt of\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{തിരിച്ചയയ്ക്കുക} (tiriccayaykkuka)}{തിരിച്ചയയ്ക്കുക (tiriccayaykkuka)}]{\ml{തിരിച്ചയയ്ക്കുക} (tiriccayaykkuka) — to send back}

\label{lesson:ML-C490-tiriccayaykkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a courier, then the Malayalam for to receive officially.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{തിരിച്ചയയ്ക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{തിരിച്ചയയ്ക്കുക}} — \emph{tiriccayaykkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to send back\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{തെറ്റായ} \ml{വിലാസം} \ml{കാരണം} \ml{തപാൽ} \ml{വകുപ്പ്} \ml{കത്ത്} \ml{തിരിച്ചയച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{teṟṟāya vilāsaṁ kāraṇaṁ tapāl vakuppŭ kattŭ tiriccayaccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Because of a wrong address, the post office sent the letter back.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{തിരിച്ചയച്ചു}, \emph{tiriccayaccu}.

\ml{തിരിച്ച്}, back, plus \ml{അയയ്ക്കുക}, to send.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{തിരിച്ചയയ്ക്കുക}} (\emph{tiriccayaykkuka}) is a native Dravidian compound of \ml{തിരിച്ച്}, back (DEDR 3246), and \ml{അയയ്ക്കുക}, to send (DEDR 37).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tiriccayaykkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tiriccayaykkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{teṟṟāya vilāsaṁ kāraṇaṁ tapāl vakuppŭ kattŭ tiriccayaccu.} — Because of a wrong address, the post office sent the letter back.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a courier, then the Malayalam for to receive officially, then say \emph{tiriccayaykkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{തിരിച്ചയയ്ക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To send back\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ബന്ധപ്പെടുക} (bandhappeṭuka)}{ബന്ധപ്പെടുക (bandhappeṭuka)}]{\ml{ബന്ധപ്പെടുക} (bandhappeṭuka) — to contact; to get in touch}

\label{lesson:ML-C490-bandhappetuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to receive officially, then the Malayalam for to send back.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ബന്ധപ്പെടുക}}
\textbf{\ml{ബന്ധപ്പെടുക}} — \emph{bandhappeṭuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to contact; to get in touch\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{പാഴ്സൽ} \ml{വൈകിയപ്പോൾ} \ml{ഞാൻ} \ml{കൊറിയർ} \ml{കമ്പനിയുമായി} \ml{ബന്ധപ്പെട്ടു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pāḻsal vaikiyappōḷ ñān koṟiyar kampaniyumāyi bandhappeṭṭu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
When the parcel was late, I got in touch with the courier company.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{ബന്ധപ്പെട്ടു}, \emph{bandhappeṭṭu}.

The one you contact takes -\ml{ഉമായി}: \ml{ബാങ്കുമായി} \ml{ബന്ധപ്പെടുക}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ബന്ധപ്പെടുക}} (\emph{bandhappeṭuka}) is built from Sanskrit \emph{bandha}, \textquotedblleft{}a tie, a bond\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with -\ml{പ്പെടുക}: to come into a tie with someone.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bandhappeṭuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bandhappeṭuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pāḻsal vaikiyappōḷ ñān koṟiyar kampaniyumāyi bandhappeṭṭu.} — When the parcel was late, I got in touch with the courier company.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to receive officially, then the Malayalam for to send back, then say \emph{bandhappeṭuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ബന്ധപ്പെടുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To contact; to get in touch\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
